name: Middle temporal gyrus, anterior division
summary: The anterior middle temporal gyrus lies between the superior and inferior temporal sulci in the front half of the lateral temporal lobe, forward of the level of the posterior insula. It is heteromodal association cortex that stores the meanings of words and the knowledge of objects and people, forming with the temporal pole the semantic system of the ventral language stream. It is supplied by the inferior division of the middle cerebral artery with a contribution from the posterior cerebral artery at its lower border, it atrophies early in semantic dementia and Alzheimer disease, and it is the lateral cortex most often included in an anterior temporal lobectomy for medial temporal epilepsy.

anatomy.location: Anterior half of the middle of the three lateral temporal gyri, bounded above by the superior temporal sulcus and below by the inferior temporal sulcus, continuous in front with the temporal pole and behind with the posterior division.

afferents.from: Fusiform and inferior temporal cortex (visual objects)

efferents.via: perforant path input via parahippocampal cortex

function: The anterior middle temporal cortex links the sound and the written form of a word with its meaning and stores knowledge about objects, animals and famous people in a modality-independent form; on the left it is essential for comprehension of single words and for naming, on the right it contributes to recognizing familiar faces and voices and to understanding social scenes and narratives. It receives the visual object stream from the fusiform and inferior temporal cortex and the auditory identification stream from the superior temporal gyrus and projects to the inferior frontal gyrus through the inferior fronto-occipital and uncinate fasciculi. Seizure spread into this cortex produces the auditory and complex auras of lateral temporal epilepsy.

bestView.label: anterior middle temporal gyrus between the superior and inferior temporal sulci
lateral temporal cortex at the level of the amygdala

imaging.normalAppearance: The middle of the three lateral temporal gyri on coronal images through the amygdala and the anterior hippocampus, separated from the superior temporal gyrus by the deep superior temporal sulcus.

pathology.finding: Asymmetric anterior temporal atrophy involving the middle and inferior temporal gyri and the temporal pole with a widened superior temporal sulcus.
Middle temporal and medial temporal atrophy with hippocampal volume loss; the lateral temporal loss follows the entorhinal and hippocampal changes.
Auditory hallucinations, vertigo or complex visual auras with an anterior temporal focus on scalp EEG.

lesionEffects.mechanism: Loss of the lexical-semantic store of the anterior middle temporal gyrus

lesionEffects.deficit: Difficulty recognizing familiar people and objects (right)
lesionEffects.mechanism: Loss of person and object knowledge in the right anterior temporal cortex
Ictal activation of lateral temporal association cortex

examination: Naming of pictures of increasing difficulty and definition of words
Picture matching by meaning (which two go together)
pearls: Semantic loss means the patient asks what a familiar word means; the speech itself stays fluent and grammatical
Anterior lateral temporal cortex is the first cortex beyond the hippocampus to atrophy in Alzheimer disease
Auditory and vertiginous auras are lateral temporal; fear and epigastric rising are medial

pitfalls: Word-finding difficulty with intact comprehension is not semantic dementia; test what the patient knows about the word they cannot find
